title: Hot-swap variant switchbench notes
content:
Goal:
- Measure user-visible cost of switching between model variants (near-compatible families) while retaining soft state (KV cache) vs full cold swap.
- Quantify transient latency, throughput dip, and KV-cache miss amplification during swap window.

Why this matters:
- Routing policies that dynamically downgrade/upgrade models (cost vs quality) need fast, low-disruption switches. We observed user-impacting regressions when switching variants during peak hours. Want concrete SLO guidance (grace windows, prewarm thresholds).

Test harness summary:
- Small cluster (3x A10g equiv) single-replica per variant. Serving runtime: rwinf/serve:main-2025-10-branch.
- Model A: llama-like open-ggml converted fp16 (base-variant).
- Model B: same topology but quantized int8 Q4 (cheap-variant).
- Invocation mix: steady 1000 qps, payload mix 75% short (64 tokens), 25% long (1024 tokens).
- Traffic generator: custom harness (bench/switchbench) that drives persistent connections and reproduces realistic interleaving.
- Measurement points: client-side p50/p95/p99, server-side scheduling queue length, KV cache hit-rate, kernel-init events, CPU/GPU utilization.
- Swap types tested: "soft-swap" (swap routing to prewarmed variant instance preserving KV by shared front-end) vs "full-swap" (drain+stop old replica, start new replica).

Commands used (snippet):
- bench: ./bench/switchbench --qps 1000 --mix short:0.75,long:0.25 --duration 900s --swap-at 300s --swap-type soft
- monitoring: /scripts/pull-metrics --since 2025-11-02T10:00 --tags hot-swap

Key timeline observations (soft-swap):
- At swap trigger (t=300s) routing switch flips ~99% of new requests to Model B within 120ms (median).
- Median latency change from baseline: +12ms. p95 increased from 38ms -> 65ms (+71%). p99 increased from 112ms -> 178ms (+59%).
- KV cache: hit-rate dropped briefly (120ms window) from 84% -> 32% as sticky sessions re-resolved; recovered to 80% within ~1.2s due to background prefix priming.
- Throughput: no sustained drop; short transient (<500ms) variance saw <3% loss of successful responses (retries increased).
- Server-side: no kernel recompile events; no GPU context eviction observed.
- CPU/GPU: CPU spike ~8% for ~300ms (routing table update + priming). GPU utilization stable.

Full-swap results:
- Swap sequence (drain old -> stop -> start new) caused a 7.2s window where tail latencies spiked.
- Median latency jump: +38ms. p95: from 42ms -> 260ms. p99: from 118ms -> 1.2s (many requests queued and retried).
- Throughput: effective drop ~22% during 7s window.
- KV cache: cold (0% hit) at start of new replica; built up over ~9s to reach 70% hit-rate for common prefixes.
- Observed kernel load overhead: initial model load triggered JIT kernel selection/dyn-alloc for attention kernels, causing the 1–3s high-p99 tail for long requests.

Interpretation / root causes:
- Soft-swap succeeds because front-end routing can redirect to an already hot variant and preserved short-lived network connections maintain some cache/context glue. The main transient is due to session re-affinity resolution and prefix re-priming.
- Full-swap pain comes from: model binary load + kernel selection + KV cold start. Even with warm disk cache, attention-kernel init and CUDA context setup add multi-second tails for certain long-context requests.
- Long requests (1k tokens) amplify tail effects because each request triggers multiple heavy kernels; if any kernel is being prepared it's multiplicative.

Quick numbers for SLO guidance (baseline SLOs: p95 < 200ms, p99 < 500ms):
- Soft-swap: meets p95 SLO (65ms) and p99 mostly OK (178ms) if we rate-limit swap events to off-peak or 5s grace windows.
- Full-swap: violates p99 (1.2s) and risks p95 for a 7s window. Avoid during peak; require circuit-breaker and dual-replica routing if unavoidable.

Recommendations (concrete):
1) Prefer soft-swap routing for intra-family variant changes. Implement pre-swap handoff that updates front-end affinity within 200ms and kicks off background prefix priming.
2) For full-swap (different model binaries): use parallel warm-start: deploy new replica, bring to READY state with synthetic priming traffic (see priming recipe), then shift traffic. Avoid drain-then-start sequence.
3) Add a small prefetch priming loop: 30s of a 10tps synthetic prefix replay targeted to top-500 prefixes forces KV population and kernel paths; empirically shortens cold recovery from ~9s -> ~1.4s.
4) Implement a swap-safety throttle: disallow full-swap if 5-min average p95 > 180ms or if total QPS > 0.8x capacity.
5) Expose a telemetry event (swap_start, swap_end, priming_hits, priming_misses) so downstream ops can correlate and surface incident pages automatically.

Notes on priming recipe (what worked):
- Sequence: start priming 12s before routing cutover. Use client-shaped requests: 80% short prompts with common prefixes + 20% long priming contexts to exercise KV warm paths.
- Throughput: 10–30 tps during priming is sufficient; higher tps wasted and causes unnecessary cost.
- Observed effect: reduces initial p99 spike by ~6x for long requests when priming completes before cutover.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Can we snapshot and transfer KV-prefix sets between replicas to avoid re-population? (tradeoff: memory + transfer time).
- Evaluate warm-start on larger model families (3B->7B switches): is kernel mismatch overhead bigger? Run scaled run.
- Investigate whether lightweight kernel pre-init (no runtime allocation) can be performed during deploy to shave the 1–3s kernel-init tail.

Appendix: raw numbers (selected)
- Baseline p50/p95/p99: 21ms / 38ms / 112ms
- Soft-swap (during 0.5s window) p50/p95/p99: 33ms / 65ms / 178ms
- Full-swap (7s window) p50/p95/p99: 59ms / 260ms / 1200ms
- KV hit-rate baseline: 84%
- KV hit-rate soft-swap nadir: 32% (120ms) -> recovered to 80% in 1.2s
- KV hit-rate full-swap: 0% -> 70% in 9s

Immediate next steps (2-week):
- Replicate experiment at 10k qps scale (staging) with larger model mixes. Owner: Luis.
- Implement priming harness integrated with rollout pipeline (PR referenced above). Owner: Anya.
- Add telemetry events to runtime and expose swap metrics in Console. Owner: Chiara (this doc).

Notes-to-self: capture real-user traffic prefixes and pick top-1k prefixes for priming set; be careful with privacy (hash prefixes, do not store full prompts).

End of scratch notes.
